findings.summary: Algorithmic risk-allocation novelty was explicitly rejected; classical allocation is treated as known machinery.
The novelty assessment rejects conditional validity from marginal quantiles and defaults to an explicit fixed-cohort event.
Request, cohort, selected outstanding-set, and budget-window events are separated in the approved framing.
Phase C must implement D007: expiry/missing telemetry carries unresolved liability rather than releasing it.
Phase C/D must use transactional outbox/inbox and claim exactly-once ledger effects, not atomic provider execution.
Phase C strict-mode assumptions must enumerate every billable token/attempt/pricing dimension and concern estimated token cost unless invoices are reconciled.
Phase C state machine must add approval, late settlement, corrections, attempts, workload UID and rollover.
Phase C invariant proof must cover every transition, not admission only.
Drift fallback is operational and does not restore statistical calibration without revalidation.
Matched-risk fixed/adaptive allocation falsifier remains frozen-design work; failure removes any optional algorithmic claim.
Phase H/J must use hierarchical independent units and state live-tail precision limits.
